source.title: EviGraph: Evidence-Guided Autonomous Research Agents
source.publication_status: ARXIV_PREPRINT; peer-reviewed venue not established by reviewed artifact

reading.scope: All supplied extracted text including references, prompts, orchestration, evaluation and expanded trace. PDF figures/layout not independently visually checked. No code or runtime reproduction.

claims.claim: Six typed research objects and five relation schemas form operational state; the graph can branch and merge, with multiple experiments/findings supporting a claim.
claims.use_limit: Supports prior architecture only; neither universal graph expressiveness nor ARGO effect.

claims.claim: The inspector localizes weak roots; content-dependent downstream nodes are removed and regenerated in dependency order, with unrelated objects preserved. The closure distinguishes content dependency from contextual reachability.
claims.use_limit: Scoped invalidation and selective downstream regeneration are direct prior art, not an ARGO novelty claim.

claims.claim: Repair uses transactional staging, checkpoints, valid-chain preservation, weak-root minimization and rollback. Append-only version records carry graph/parent hashes, actions, validation, preserved-chain IDs, costs and execution references.
claims.use_limit: The specified rollback mechanism is not demonstrated by the representative case; no independently reproduced runtime claim.

claims.claim: Long-term memory admits evidence-ready graphs and improving repair traces; retrieval supplies advisory structures and requires current-run evidence instead of copying prior findings/claims/values.
claims.use_limit: Prior experience revalidation is already described. The paper does not by itself validate ARGO applicability rules or generalized negative-knowledge transfer.

claims.claim: Contracts validate structure/provenance and require a nonempty retained-claim set and required deliverables; invalid Problem/Gap anchors trigger reinitialization. Negative results are retained as findings and scoped negative claims or unsupported hypotheses.
claims.use_limit: The abstract claim of all retained claims being graph-grounded is a method guard, not perfect semantic correctness or 100% independent CSR.

claims.claim: Writing is graph-grounded through a paragraph skeleton and span-level provenance map; review checks structure, novelty framing, citations and graph faithfulness, with budgeted revision and incomplete outcomes.
claims.use_limit: Evidence-gated writing and provenance mapping are direct prior art. No originality/accuracy guarantee.

claims.claim: Evaluation compares two systems on 25 ARC-Bench-ML and 20 NanoResearch tasks with a common qwen-3.6-plus backbone, sandbox and per-experiment time budget; native scores and added reliability metrics are distinct.
claims.use_limit: Comparison population is these systems/tasks/settings, not all current research agents or ARGO.

claims.claim: The paper reports CSR 37.85% versus 27% for the strongest CSR baseline: +10.85 percentage points, or 40.19% relative. EDC is 87.73%, below NanoResearch 96.15%; alignment also trails NanoResearch.
claims.use_limit: Do not convert the relative CSR gain into percentage points, call all metrics best, use as local effect/power prior, or imply all claims verified.

claims.claim: The paper declines conventional component ablation because components are coupled, using qualitative alignment and a representative trace instead. The trace exercises neither rollback nor long-term retrieval.
claims.use_limit: Aggregate gains do not identify the contribution of graph topology, repair, filtering, writing gates, rollback or cross-run memory separately.

claims.claim: The specification applies one accounting policy to planning/model/tool/retry costs across systems. The text fixes per-experiment limits and requires manifests for hardware, sampling, seeds, counts and token/tool/runtime totals.
claims.use_limit: It is false to say no cost accounting is specified. Equal total caps, realized total costs, code revisions and repetition counts are not established by the inspected extracted paper; required audit fields are not supplied values.

claims.claim: Reliability evaluation freezes extraction configuration, preserves occurrence-based denominators, blinds system identities/field names, normalizes evidence classes, rejects bare graph labels as evidence, and uses a frozen numerical matching policy.
claims.use_limit: Do not call the protocol unblinded or purely self-certified. The extracted paper does not provide validation of actual blinding effectiveness or human calibration.

claims.claim: Claim/value extraction and support/match membership are LLM-mediated; ratio calculation is external. Two independent agent reviewers are described for native ARC scoring, not established independent human or distinct-model validation for every reliability decision.
claims.use_limit: LLM categorical judgments remain fallible. Exact evaluator/extractor identities, inter-rater reliability and human-adjudicated accuracy are unresolved in the reviewed text.

claims.claim: Graph readiness quantifies over retained current-run graph claims, while external CSR extraction includes broader manuscript propositions and stochastic occurrence-level denominators; these are different scopes.
claims.use_limit: CSR below 100% is not by itself a logical contradiction of the internal readiness predicate. Scope-sensitive denominator and evaluator error audits are still needed.

claims.claim: The two-baseline whole-system comparison leaves alternative explanations through hypothesis filtering, inspection/repair, gate/writer behavior, and resource utilization. It does not compare a strong persistent source-backed tree with equal evidence rights, obligations and enforcement.
claims.use_limit: This is a causal-identification limitation, not proof the baselines are intrinsically weak or EviGraph ineffective.

claims.claim: The paper text supplies aggregate point estimates and required run-record fields, but not uncertainty intervals or visible raw reliability counts alongside Table 4. Actual manifests/raw outputs were not inspected in this review.
claims.use_limit: Do not infer zero replications or absent artifacts; only uncertainty and denominator auditability are unverified from this text.

bcg_comparison.B: Strong persistent source-backed tree/notebook; advisory applicability/revalidation/preservation/recovery; same source facts, rights, budget and safety/measurement rules.
bcg_comparison.C: Same evidence and rights, compulsory research checks; C-B tests obligation/process package.
bcg_comparison.G: Same obligations/enforcement as C plus graph-mediated dependency traversal, scoped invalidation and continuation; G-C tests a graph-control package, not pure topology.
overlap: content-dependent descendant closure and scoped regeneration
advisory prior experience with current-run revalidation
provenance, version hashes and append-only checkpoints
atomic repair, rollback and preservation of existing valid evidence
non-vacuous manuscript gating and provenance-mapped writing
bcg_comparison.residual: A prospective causal comparison against a strong persistent tree/notebook with matched evidence rights, compulsory obligations, enforcement and total resource caps, assessed using a preselected single final artifact and independent hidden scoring. This is a candidate empirical contribution, not proven methodological novelty or efficacy.
required_design_implications: Preserve strong tree-plus-insight and equal evidence/recovery access in B/C/G.
Keep filtering, repair/writing obligations and scheduling common or separately identify their interventions.
Count all planning, retries, verification, tool calls and graph maintenance in total cost; retain incomplete runs.
Freeze evaluator identities, blind normalized evidence and independently audit claim/value denominators.
Evaluate scoped invalidation/recovery with held-out boundary cases but retain final-artifact outcome as primary.
Separate operational negative-result preservation from new knowledge-transfer/applicability hypotheses; the former already appears here.
bcg_comparison.current_state_limit: Current P0 is C0 feasibility, with no observed assigned B/C/G programme; no experiment/native implementation changes authorized by this review.
